belief: My suffering means God has abandoned me.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that your suffering means God has abandoned you, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Long seasons of pain without relief. Prayers that seem unanswered. Feeling alone in your suffering. Believing God’s presence should always bring comfort and ease. Past experiences of being abandoned by people you trusted.
teaches: Suffering can make God feel far away, but Scripture promises He is with you in it. God says that when you pass through the waters and walk through the fire, He will be with you. Nothing—trouble, distress, persecution, or danger—can separate you from the love of Christ. Even if a mother could forget her child, God will not forget you; He has written you on the palms of His hands. Your suffering is not a sign of abandonment, but a place where God promises to be present.
self_statements: God has left me alone in this.
If God were with me, I wouldn’t be suffering.
No one, not even God, cares.
errors: Concluding “I feel abandoned, so God must have left.”
Turning a season of pain into “God has left me forever.”
Assuming God abandons like people have.
Overlooking God’s promises to be present in suffering.
questions: What does God promise in Isaiah 43:2 about the waters and the fire?
Can trouble or distress separate me from Christ’s love?
What has God written on the palms of His hands?
Am I picturing God like people who abandoned me?
Did faithful people in Scripture suffer while God was with them?
What small signs of God’s care can I see?
Can I trust His promise more than my feelings?
truth: My suffering does not mean God has abandoned me. He promises to be with me through the waters and the fire. Nothing can separate me from the love of Christ. God has not forgotten me; I am written on the palms of His hands. He is with me in the valley.

log: Each day, write one small sign that God has not abandoned me.
name_example: When Sarah passes through the waters, I will be with her; and when she goes through the rivers, they will not overwhelm her. When she walks through the fire, she will not be scorched; the flames will not set her ablaze.
actions: Write your name on your palm or a card
and tell them you are struggling.
and notice where God is in the valley.
tracker: One sign God has not left me
prayer: Father, sometimes I feel abandoned in my suffering. Help me reject the lie that You have left me. Thank You that You are with me through the waters and the fire, that nothing can separate me from Your love, and that I am written on the palms of Your hands. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
